claims: Artemis III is currently targeted for launch in mid-2027, according to NASA.
Artemis III will be a crewed mission aimed at testing rendezvous and docking capabilities with commercial landers in low-Earth orbit.
As of April 2026, Artemis III launch date is scheduled for 2027.
As reported by Space.com, the Artemis III crew will launch on the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket in the Orion spacecraft.
As reported by Space.com, the Artemis III crew will dock with a commercial lander such as SpaceX’s Starship in low-Earth orbit.
As reported by Space.com, Artemis III does not immediately land on the Moon.
SpaceNews and The Guardian note that the Artemis III mission revision follows concerns over technological readiness.
SpaceNews and The Guardian note that the revision focuses on addressing delays in the human landing system (HLS).
The actual human lunar landing has been shifted to the Artemis IV mission.
Artemis IV mission is now targeted for 2028.
